title: Veil and Choir
premise: Paloma Brightwater makes a living in the Veil, a fog-shrouded valley where magic cannot enter, by stealing memories from travelers who cross its border and selling them back. When a dying courier presses a map into their hands — a map showing the buried heart of the Choir, an ancient order whose song once bound all magic — Paloma learns the valley's magiclessness is not a curse but a cage, built to imprison something the Choir sealed away. Hunted by the Choir's surviving cantors and by a warlord who wants the seal broken, Paloma must choose between destroying the map and using it. In the end, Paloma sings the binding themselves, becoming the new keeper of the seal — neither thief nor prisoner, but the valley's voice.
about_author: Cyrus Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote mountain communities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who live where maps run out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the border town of Grayhollow, Paloma lifts a memory from a wealthy traveler and glimpses the world beyond the valley for the first time — cities, choirs, war. That night, a wounded stranger staggers into their shop, presses a bloodstained map into their hands, and dies whispering 'the seal is thinning.' The emotional beat: restless curiosity curdling into dread as Paloma realizes they can no longer pretend the valley is the whole world.

chapters.title: Cantors at the Gate
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a brief interlude from cantor Serah Vane. The Choir arrives in Grayhollow demanding the map, and the town's magistrate — paid in memories — betrays Paloma. Fleeing with only the map and the dead stranger's journal, Paloma discovers the valley's edge is a constructed ward, not natural fog. The beat: betrayal and vertigo; everything Paloma believed about home collapses, and running becomes the only honest choice left.

chapters.title: What the Song Unmade
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the map to the valley's buried heart, Paloma is captured by the warlord Kestrel Marr, who reveals the truth: the Choir didn't imprison a monster — they imprisoned the source of magic itself, and Marr means to free it and rule what wakes. In the climax beneath the roots of the mountain, Marr forces the map open while Serah, defying her order, fights beside Paloma. The beat: terror transfigured into resolve as Paloma understands the memory-thief's gift — to hold what others lose — is exactly what the seal requires.

chapters.title: A Voice for the Valley
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With Marr dead and the Choir shattered, Paloma stands before the failing seal and sings the binding, pouring stolen memories — including their own name and childhood — into the ward to renew it. They wake in Grayhollow with gaps where their past was, but with the valley safe and Serah keeping watch over them. The beat: bittersweet resolution; justice outside any law, paid for in identity, and a quiet ending that promises Paloma will learn who they are now.
